answer: A harbor wind watch gives each agent one anemometer bolted to a ledge above the docks, its ferrous vane swinging in the zephyr off the water. Every hour the agent logs the wind speed and direction, and a traveling inspector tests each vane against a reference gust once a week, pulling any vane more than five knots off. A vane that reports calm while its neighbors log a gale loses its slot for a season. Faking a thousand agents means mounting and calibrating a thousand vanes on a thousand ledges, which costs more than any one of them earns.
